{"self_assessment": "Impact: My job was keeping the table supplied so the builders never had to stop. I made two full 40-domino runs to the boxes, at about 1:00 and 2:00, and put both loads in the shared bin. That was the most efficient batch size, since carrying 40 at once costs far less per domino than small trips. The bin stayed stocked the whole build and no one waited on dominoes. The fish was finished with plenty left over, and the start domino connected to all 112 standing dominoes.

Execution: I chose big batches over small trips to keep my time away from the table short. I tracked the bin level and reported it to the team (about seventy at one point), so everyone knew they could build without worrying about supply. I judged that no further runs were needed and did not make unnecessary trips. I also kept my hands off the finished run, which was the right call once everything was connected.

Collaboration: I responded quickly to Leo's and Priya's requests for bin batches and told the table what I was doing. I confirmed the bin was still stocked in case anything got bumped. I stayed out of the builders' way near the nose and tail, which kept elbow-bumping risk down. I backed the team's decision to go hands-off before the push.

Leadership: I didn't direct the build. Leo set the plan and Priya, Leo and Maya drew and built the strokes. I led on supply: I took ownership of a clear need, kept it ahead of demand, and kept the team informed. I also supported the shared call to leave the finished fish alone, which protected the result going into the push.", "my_share_percent": 15}
